sections.title: Level 2 Figure Series Strategy
sections.content: In Level 2, multiple changes may occur at the same time. Step 1: Break the entire figure into separate elements. Step 2: Observe the pattern of each element individually. Step 3: Check whether the pattern is continuous or alternating. Step 4: Compare 3 or 4 figures to confirm the rule.

sections.title: Multi-element Series
sections.content: Step 1: Identify all symbols present in the figure. Step 2: Observe the movement or transformation of each symbol separately. Step 3: Identify the direction (clockwise or anti-clockwise). Step 4: Check for changes in shading or orientation. Example: If Symbol A rotates clockwise, Symbol B rotates anti-clockwise, and Symbol C changes shading in every step, the next figure will follow the same sequence.

sections.title: Alternating Series Pattern
sections.content: Step 1: Identify the rule from Step 1 to Step 2. Step 2: Observe the rule from Step 2 to Step 3. Step 3: Check whether the first rule repeats from Step 3 to Step 4. Step 4: Confirm the alternating pattern. Example: The first step may involve rotation and the second step may involve addition, and this sequence repeats.

sections.title: Appearance and Disappearance Pattern
sections.content: Step 1: Observe whether new symbols are appearing or existing ones are disappearing. Step 2: Identify whether this happens in every step or in alternate steps. Step 3: Observe the position of the new symbol (corner, center, etc.). Step 4: Understand the sequence of both removal and addition. Example: In every second step, a new symbol appears in the top-right corner while an old symbol disappears.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Trying to explain all symbols using a single rule. 2. Failing to recognize alternating patterns. 3. Ignoring shading or orientation changes. 4. Not considering addition and movement together.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: In Level 2 figure series, multiple elements may change simultaneously. Different symbols may follow different rules. Alternating patterns and appearance–disappearance patterns must be identified carefully.

tricks.title: Element Separation Trick
tricks.explanation: Divide the entire figure into different symbols and analyze the pattern of each one.
tricks.example: A dot may rotate while the shading of a triangle changes.

tricks.title: Direction Check Method
tricks.explanation: Identify the movement direction of each symbol.
tricks.example: One symbol may move clockwise while another moves anti-clockwise.

tricks.title: Alternating Rule Identification
tricks.explanation: Observe the difference between Step 1→2 and Step 2→3.
tricks.example: First rotation, then addition, and then rotation repeats.

tricks.title: Corner Pattern Trick
tricks.explanation: If a new symbol appears in alternate steps, focus on the corners.
tricks.example: The symbol may appear in top-left → top-right → bottom-right sequence.

tricks.title: Shading Observation
tricks.explanation: Sometimes only the shading changes while the shape remains the same.
tricks.example: An empty circle may become filled in the next figure.

tricks.title: Alternate Step Comparison
tricks.example: If they look similar, the pattern is likely alternating.

tricks.title: Addition-Deletion Balance
tricks.explanation: If one symbol is being added, another may be removed.
tricks.example: A new symbol appears in a corner while the center symbol disappears.

tricks.title: Movement Track Method
tricks.explanation: Mentally track the movement of a symbol across the series.
tricks.example: A dot may move to the next corner in each step.
